arxiv-2012-02225.title: Size and structures of disks around very low mass stars in the Taurus star-forming region
arxiv-2012-02225.creator: N. T. Kurtovic, P. Pinilla, F. Long, M. Benisty, C. F Manara, A. Natta, I. Pascucci, L. Ricci A. Scholz, L. Testi
arxiv-2012-02225.description: Abstract Context. The discovery of giant planets orbiting very low mass stars (VLMS) and the recent observed substructures in disks around VLMS is challenging planet formation models. Aims. We aim to estimate if structures, such as cavities, rings, and gaps, are common in disks around VLMS and to test models of structure formation in these disks.

arxiv-2210-09611.title: Relationships between patenting trends and research activity for green energy technologies
arxiv-2210-09611.creator: Regina TUGANOVA, Anna PERMYAKOVA, Anna KUZNETSOVA, Karina RAKHMANOVA, Natalia MONZUL, Roman UVAROV, Elizaveta KOVTUN, Semen BUDENNYY
arxiv-2210-09611.description: Abstract Green technology is viewed as a means of creating a sustainable society and a catalyst for sustainable development by the global community. It is responsible for both the potential reduction of production waste and the reduction of carbon footprint and CO 2 emissions.

arxiv-2302-01800.title: Creating Probabilistic Forecasts from Arbitrary Deterministic Forecasts using Conditional Invertible Neural Networks Journal: International Journal of Forecasting
arxiv-2302-01800.creator: Kaleb Phipps, Benedikt Heidrich, Marian Turowski, Moritz Wittig, Ralf Mikut, Veit Hagenmeyer
arxiv-2302-01800.description: Abstract In various applications, probabilistic forecasts are required to quantify the inherent uncertainty associated with the forecast. However, numerous modern forecasting methods are still designed to create deterministic forecasts. Transforming these deterministic forecasts into probabilistic forecasts is often challenging and based on numerous assumptions that may not hold in real-world situations.

arxiv-2401-02179.title: On two open questions for extension bundles Thanks: ∗ the corresponding author
arxiv-2401-02179.creator: Qiang Dong, Shiquan Ruan ∗
arxiv-2401-02179.description: Abstract . In this paper we give positive answers for two open questions on extension bundles over weighted projective lines, raised by Kussin, Lenzing and Meltzer in the paper “Triangle singularities, ADE-chains and weighted projective lines”. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 14H60, 16G60, 16G70, 18G80 1.

arxiv-2404-00415.title: CoDa: Constrained Generation based Data Augmentation for Low-Resource NLP
arxiv-2404-00415.creator: Chandra Kiran Evuru, Sreyan Ghosh, Sonal Kumar, Ramaneswaran S, Utkarsh Tyagi, Dinesh Manocha
arxiv-2404-00415.description: Abstract We present CoDa ( Co nstrained Generation based Da ta Augmentation), a controllable, effective, and training-free data augmentation technique for low-resource (data-scarce) NLP. Our approach is based on prompting off-the-shelf instruction-following Large Language Models (LLMs) for generating text that satisfies a set of constraints.

arxiv-2408-11440.title: Lahaja : A Robust Multi-accent Benchmark for Evaluating Hindi ASR Systems
arxiv-2408-11440.creator: Tahir Javed, Janki Nawale, Sakshi Joshi, Eldho George, Kaushal Bhogale, Deovrat Mehendale, Mitesh M. Khapra
arxiv-2408-11440.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tahir Javed, Janki Nawale, Sakshi Joshi, Eldho George, Kaushal Bhogale, Deovrat Mehendale, Mitesh M. Khapra. Hindi, one of the most spoken language of India, exhibits a diverse array of accents due to its usage among individuals from diverse linguistic origins.

arxiv-2508-15236.title: Pathology-Informed Latent Diffusion Model for Anomaly Detection in Lymph Node Metastasis
arxiv-2508-15236.creator: Jiamu Wang, Keunho Byeon, Jinsol Song, Anh Nguyen, Sangjeong Ahn, Sung Hak Lee ∗, Jin Tae Kwak ∗
arxiv-2508-15236.description: Abstract Anomaly detection is an emerging approach in digital pathology for its ability to efficiently and effectively utilize data for disease diagnosis. While supervised learning approaches deliver high accuracy, they rely on extensively annotated datasets, suffering from data scarcity in digital pathology.

arxiv-2510-19176.title: The Zero-Step Thinking: An Empirical Study of Mode Selection as Harder Early Exit in Reasoning Models
arxiv-2510-19176.creator: Yuqiao Tan, Shizhu He, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao
arxiv-2510-19176.description: Abstract Reasoning models have demonstrated exceptional performance in tasks such as mathematics and logical reasoning, primarily due to their ability to engage in step-by-step thinking during the reasoning process. However, this often leads to overthinking, resulting in unnecessary computational overhead.

arxiv-2511-14651.title: Derivative of the truncated singular value and eigen decomposition
arxiv-2511-14651.creator: Jan Naumann
arxiv-2511-14651.description: Abstract Recently developed applications in the field of machine learning and computational physics rely on automatic differentiation techniques, that require stable and efficient linear algebra gradient computations. This technical note provides a comprehensive and detailed discussion of the derivative of the truncated singular and eigenvalue decomposition.

plos-pone-0008428.title: Glucose Metabolism, Islet Architecture, and Genetic Homogeneity in Imprinting of [Ca 2+ ] i and Insulin Rhythms in Mouse Islets
plos-pone-0008428.creator: Craig S. Nunemaker, John F. Dishinger, Stacey B. Dula et al.
plos-pone-0008428.description: PLOS ONE research article. We reported previously that islets isolated from individual, outbred Swiss-Webster mice displayed oscillations in intracellular calcium ([Ca 2+ ] i ) that varied little between islets of a single mouse but considerably between mice, a phenomenon we termed “islet imprinting.” We h

pmc-10612407.title: Privacy-preserving federated genome-wide association studies via dynamic sampling
pmc-10612407.creator: Xinyue Wang, Leonard Dervishi, Wentao Li, Erman Ayday, Xiaoqian Jiang, Jaideep Vaidya, Macha Nikolski
pmc-10612407.description: MotivationGenome-wide association studies (GWAS) benefit from the increasing availability of genomic data and cross-institution collaborations. However, sharing data across institutional boundaries jeopardizes medical data confidentiality and patient privacy. While modern cryptographic techniques provide formal secure guarantees, the substantial communication and computational overheads hinder the practical application of large-scale collaborative GWAS.

pmc-11513196.title: A network analysis of affective and motivational individual differences and error monitoring in a non-clinical sample
pmc-11513196.creator: Anna Grabowska, Filip Sondej, Magdalena Senderecka
pmc-11513196.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Error monitoring, which plays a crucial role in shaping adaptive behavior, is influenced by a complex interplay of affective and motivational factors. Understanding these associations often proves challenging due to the intricate nature of these variables. With the aim of addressing previous inconsistencies and methodological gaps, in this study, we utilized network analysis to investigate the relationship between affective and motivational individual differences and error monitoring.

pmc-11555662.title: Effects of Approved Pharmacological Interventions for Insomnia on Mood Disorders: A Systematic Review
pmc-11555662.creator: Laura Palagini, Mario Miniati, Donatella Marazziti, Dieter Riemann, Pierre A Geoffroy, Angelo Gemignani
pmc-11555662.description: ObjectiveInsomnia can be a contributing factor, a comorbid disorder, or a transdiagnostic element to several mental disorders, including mood disorders (MDs). A recent meta-analysis has already shown the effectiveness of cognitive behavioral treatment (CBT) for insomnia that is comorbid with MDs. This work aimed to systematically review data on pharmacological insomnia treatment in the context of MDS.

pmc-11630640.title: Determination of metal ion transport rate of human ZIP4 using stable zinc isotopes
pmc-11630640.creator: Yuhan Jiang, Keith MacRenaris, Thomas V O’Halloran, Jian Hu
pmc-11630640.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The essential microelement zinc is absorbed in the small intestine mainly by the zinc transporter ZIP4, a representative member of the Zrt/Irt-like protein (ZIP) family. ZIP4 is reportedly upregulated in many cancers, making it a promising oncology drug target. To date, there have been no reports on the turnover number of ZIP4, which is a crucial missing piece of information needed to better understand the transport mechanism.

pmc-11673788.title: Nano-Delivery Revolution: Harnessing Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes’ Potential for Wound Healing
pmc-11673788.creator: Pawan Kumar Raghav, Zoya Mann, M R Mozafari, Christian Morsczeck
pmc-11673788.description: Stem cell transplantation has proven effective in treating acute and chronic wounds, but its limitations, such as low cellular viability and the need for specialized transportation, highlight the necessity for alternative approaches. This review explores the potential of engineered exosomes, containing identified miRNAs/peptides, as a more stable and efficient cell-free therapy for regenerative medicine, particularly in wound healing.

pmc-12408365.title: Comparative Assessment of Whole Organ Tissue Processing Methods for the Isolation of Extracellular Vesicles From Intact Organs
pmc-12408365.creator: Mohammed Tayab Hussain, Shani Austin‐Williams, Joel McCay, Hedayatullah Hayat, Thomas D Wright, Marilena Christoforou, Ella Ykema, Mauro Perretti, Dianne Cooper, Andreas Margraf
pmc-12408365.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are small anuclear cellular membrane encapsulated fragments of importance for cellular interaction and transfer of information. These small vesicles, diverse in size and functionality, can be obtained from cells, tissues and bodily fluids. A complicated step for obtaining EVs from whole organs is understanding the optimal methodology for organ processing.

pmc-12595940.title: Restorative Neurostimulation for Patients with Mechanical Chronic Low Back Pain and Impaired Neuromuscular Control of the Lumbar Spine | A New Treatment Paradigm
pmc-12595940.creator: Christopher J Gilligan, Avinash S Chavda, Johnson S Ho, David W Lee, Meredith Langhorst, Erika T Yih, Marco Amann
pmc-12595940.description: Chronic low back pain (CLBP) is a symptom of an underlying pathology. There are distinct phenotypes of CLBP, including neuropathic, nociplastic and nociceptive, or mechanical CLBP. We present a comprehensive clinical overview of restorative neurostimulation for refractory, disabling, mechanical CLBP.

pmc-13372175.title: Association of mainly vegetarian and vegan diets with loneliness, social isolation and social withdrawal in a German population survey
pmc-13372175.creator: André Hajek, Razak M. Gyasi, Supa Pengpid, Karl Peltzer, Karel Kostev, Pinar Soysal, Ashwin Kotwal, Lee Smith, Dong Keon Yon, Hans-Helmut König
pmc-13372175.description: AimThere is a very limited number of studies examining how diet is associated with social factors. The aim of this study was therefore to examine the association between type of diet and loneliness, social isolation and social withdrawal.MethodsCross-sectional data from the general adult population in Germany were used. The sample included 5,000 individuals aged 18–74 years.

pmc-13500833.title: Evolutionary trajectory of microbial sulfur oxidation pathways recapitulates Earth’s oxygenation history
pmc-13500833.creator: Xin-Yue Ren, Xian-Yong Lin, Tomohisa Sebastian Tanabe, Alexander Loy, Lingfei Hu, Yong-Guan Zhu, Song-Can Chen
pmc-13500833.description: Dissimilatory sulfur oxidation mediated by the microbial sulfur-oxidizing (Sox) multienzyme complex has played a central role in Earth’s oxidative sulfur cycle. However, the evolutionary trajectory leading to its current complexity remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated expanded genomic records with geochemical evidence to reconstruct the natural history of the Sox system along a geological timeline.
